question: Does a causal, diagonal Kalman innovation summary over all 112 inputs produce a nondegenerate sequence-local change clock worth testing as a GRU input?

features.warmup_scale: per-sequence sample standard deviation of input rows 0..98, floored at 1e-6
features.filter: independent scalar random-walk Kalman filter per standardized input channel
features.innovation: pre-update residual divided by sqrt(predicted state variance + R), clipped to [-8, 8]
features.row_summary: sqrt(mean(clipped standardized innovation squared across 112 channels))
features.clock: CUSUM c_t = clip(max(0, 0.95*c_(t-1) + row_summary - 1), 0, 20); appended candidate is log1p(c_t)
features.sequence_reset: all level, variance and CUSUM state is initialized inside each sequence transform

selection.membership: one complete row group from each of 32 distinct components in fold0 fit.train; no evaluation groups

interpretation.success: A stable, nondegenerate clock with meaningful time- or feature-group variation may justify a separate matched supervised endpoint screen; this feature-only diagnostic is not quality evidence.
interpretation.weak_result: Defer this exact all-channel scalarization; keep richer per-channel learned Kalman state and other causal feature arms open.
interpretation.uncertainty: Only 32 fit-side components are sampled. No labels, masks, endpoint fit, scored validation or clean-fold claim is included.
